description: Epic maturity: Reopen terminal recovery, batch issue membership, list search/sort, and a persisted activity timeline.

tasks.title: Epic events store and persistence infrastructure
tasks.description: Add a dedicated EpicEvents table via an EF Core migration mirroring IssueEventRow (PK (Source, Id), IX_EpicEvents_Type_Source_Id). Add EpicEventPersistence (SourcePrefix "/mohist/epics/"), extend EventStore.AppendAsync with a third source-prefix branch that assigns the per-source monotonic sequence id, and add IEventStore.ListEpicEventsAsync. Implement EpicEventSerializer (mirror of IssueEventSerializer) for the existing EpicEvent variants and register them in EventCatalog. Finally, give EpicGrain an IEventStore dependency and replace the no-op ApplyPendingEvents drain with post-commit best-effort persistence (capture PendingEvents, ClearPendingEvents, SaveChangesAsync, then append each via IEventStore with try/catch logging), using the injected TimeProvider for envelope timestamps so every current mutation path (create/update/priority/status/close/single link-unlink) persists instead of drains.
acceptanceCriteria: EF Core migration 'AddEpicEvents' creates an EpicEvents table with columns analogous to IssueEventRow, PK (Source, Id), and index IX_EpicEvents_Type_Source_Id
After any epic mutation (create, field update, priority change, status transition, close, single issue link/unlink) the recorded event is retrievable via IEventStore.ListEpicEventsAsync
EpicGrain no longer drains via ClearPendingEvents; it captures pending events, persists state, then appends each event through IEventStore wrapped in try/catch with _log.LogError on failure
Persisted event envelope time equals the injected TimeProvider Now(), verified under a fake TimeProvider at a fixed instant
Per-epic event sequence id (Id within a Source) increases monotonically across multiple events for one epic
EpicCreated event is persisted on epic creation with the creation timestamp
EpicEventSerializer round-trips every existing EpicEvent variant to its com.mohist.epic.* CloudEvents type string and back
Existing single-issue link/unlink behavior and default list ordering are unchanged (regression check)
Unit/spec tests pass: npm test (server) covers persistence, sequence, no-drain, fake-TimeProvider timestamps, and serializer round-trip
tasks.output: AddEpicEvents migration; EpicEventRow, EpicEventPersistence, EpicEventSerializer, EventStore epics-prefix branch, IEventStore.ListEpicEventsAsync, EventCatalog registrations, EpicGrain IEventStore persistence wiring; accompanying unit + spec tests
tasks.notes: This is the foundation: T-002 (EpicReopened variant + reopen event recording), T-003 (batch link/unlink event recording), and T-005 (timeline read path) all build on the store + persistence wired here. Existing EpicEvent variants only; the EpicReopened variant is added by T-002 to avoid dead serializer code.

tasks.title: Reopen terminal epics to idle with active-membership re-claim
tasks.description: Add an Epic.Reopen(DateTime? now) domain transition (Done/Closed -> Idle) guarded by a new EpicNotTerminalException (mirror of EnsureNotTerminal) so EnsureNotTerminal still blocks every other transition out of terminal states. Reopen records two events: EpicStatusChanged (terminal -> idle) and a new EpicReopened variant added to the EpicEvent union, EpicEventSerializer, and EventCatalog. Implement EpicGrain.ReopenAsync that, after the transition, re-establishes active memberships by checking GetActiveMembershipOwnerAsync per linked issue and inserting EpicActiveIssueRow only when no other non-terminal epic actively owns it (re-homed issues are skipped silently, never blocking reopen). Add POST /api/projects/{projectRef}/epics/{id}/reopen returning EpicDto (409 EPIC_NOT_TERMINAL on non-terminal, 404 on missing; {id} accepts internal id or number). On the web, make primaryLifecycleAction return { kind: 'reopen-epic' } for Done/Closed (null otherwise unchanged) and render a Reopen control on EpicDetailPage that calls the endpoint and invalidates epic queries on success.
acceptanceCriteria: Reopen on a done or closed epic transitions it to idle and the epic is no longer terminal
Reopen on an idle/running/paused epic throws EpicNotTerminalException and the epic's state is unchanged
POST /{id}/reopen on a non-terminal epic returns HTTP 409 with a distinct terminal-guard error code; on a missing epic returns HTTP 404; {id} accepts internal id or number
Reopen re-establishes EpicActiveIssues for every linked issue not actively owned by another non-terminal epic
A linked issue re-homed to another non-terminal epic during the terminal period is skipped (not re-claimed) and does not block reopen or the re-claim of the remaining issues
Reopen records and persists both an EpicReopened event and an EpicStatusChanged event (terminal -> idle), retrievable via the events read path
Web detail page shows a Reopen control only for terminal epics; invoking it transitions the epic to idle and refreshes the epic + linked-issue queries; non-terminal epics show no Reopen control
EnsureNotTerminal still blocks Start/Pause/Resume/Done/Close from terminal states (regression)
Unit/spec tests pass (server + web typecheck/test) covering the domain transition, grain re-claim incl. re-homed skip, HTTP codes, event recording, and web action rendering
tasks.output: Epic.Reopen + EpicNotTerminalException; EpicReopened variant in EpicEvent union + EpicEventSerializer mapping + EventCatalog entry; EpicGrain.ReopenAsync membership re-claim; POST /{id}/reopen route; web primaryLifecycleAction reopen branch + EpicDetailPage Reopen control + query invalidation; tests
tasks.notes: Depends on T-001 for the IEventStore-backed persistence path so the newly recorded EpicReopened/EpicStatusChanged events are actually stored rather than drained.

tasks.title: Batch link/unlink epic issues with per-issue outcomes
tasks.description: Add IEpicGrain.LinkIssuesAsync and UnlinkIssuesAsync taking resolved { issueId, issueNumber } pairs and returning IReadOnlyList<BatchMembershipOutcome>. The grain de-duplicates the input and processes each issue through the existing single-issue GetActiveMembershipOwnerAsync invariant, producing per-issue outcomes (linked | already-linked | conflict(owningEpicId,title) | not-found for link; unlinked | was-not-a-member for unlink) with partial-failure semantics: a single batch never throws on an individual conflict or not-found. Add HTTP POST /{id}/issues:batch and POST /{id}/issues:batch-unlink accepting { issueIds: string[] }, resolving each number/id exactly as the single-issue route does today, and returning HTTP 200 { results: BatchMembershipOutcome[] }. The existing single POST /{id}/issues and DELETE /{id}/issues/{issueId} remain unchanged. Add web api client methods batchAddEpicIssues / batchRemoveEpicIssues.
acceptanceCriteria: Batch link with [A,B,C] (none currently members) links all three and each appears in the epic's linked-issue set
Batch link resolves a mix of issue numbers and internal ids and links all resolved issues
An issue actively owned by another non-terminal epic is reported as conflict identifying the owning epic and is NOT linked; the other issues in the batch still link (no rollback)
An issue already a member of this epic is reported as already-linked (idempotent, no duplicate membership)
An issue whose epic memberships are all terminal is claimed without a duplicate-memberships conflict
An identifier resolving to no issue is reported as not-found; the other resolvable issues still link
Duplicate identifiers within one request are de-duplicated (linked at most once, not treated as an error)
Batch unlink removes exactly the requested members; an identifier that is not a member is reported was-not-a-member without error; remaining members stay linked
Both batch endpoints return HTTP 200 with one outcome entry per requested identifier; existing single link/unlink endpoints are unchanged
Unit/spec tests pass (server) covering outcomes, partial failure, dedup, idempotency, invariant, and the HTTP contract
tasks.output: IEpicGrain.LinkIssuesAsync/UnlinkIssuesAsync + BatchMembershipOutcome; EpicGrain batch processing; POST /{id}/issues:batch and :batch-unlink routes + request/response DTOs; web api client methods; tests
tasks.notes: Depends on T-001 so the batch mutation paths use the new capture/clear/save/append persistence pattern (IssueLinked/IssueUnlinked events are recorded). Reuses the existing single-issue invariant GetActiveMembershipOwnerAsync unchanged.

tasks.title: Epic list title search and sort
tasks.description: Extend EpicQuerier.ListAsync to (projectId, string? search, string? sortBy, string? sortDir). Add a bound LIKE parameter (LOWER(title) LIKE LOWER('%' || @search || '%')) for case-insensitive title substring filtering, and select the ORDER BY fragment from a small enum-bound map ((priority,asc) -> Priority ASC, UpdatedAt DESC; (updated,desc) -> UpdatedAt DESC, Priority ASC; etc.) — never raw string interpolation, so the sort is injection-safe. With no params the SQL and ordering are byte-identical to today. Forward ?search=&sort=priority|updated&dir=asc|desc on GET /api/projects/{projectRef}/epics, falling back to the default ordering on unknown values (no 400). On the web, extend useEpics with { search?, sort?, dir? } in its query key and render a search input plus a sort control on EpicListPage that drive the query; the status grouping continues to operate on the filtered/sorted result.
acceptanceCriteria: search='auth' returns only epics whose title contains 'auth' (case-insensitive)
No search term returns all epics in the project with no title filtering
sort=priority&dir=asc orders epics priority ascending (p0 before p4); sort=updated&dir=desc orders most-recently-updated first
No sort parameters yields priority ascending then updated-at descending — identical to the previous hardcoded ordering (regression-safe)
A request combining search with sort applies both the filter and the requested ordering without interference
Unknown sort or dir values fall back to the default ordering without returning HTTP 400
The web list page search box filters the list and the sort control reorders it; status grouping is preserved on the filtered/sorted set
Unit/spec tests pass (server + web typecheck/test) covering querier params (bound + injection-safe), route forwarding/fallback, and web controls
tasks.output: EpicQuerier.ListAsync search/sort signature + parameterized SQL + ORDER BY fragment map; GET / epics query-string forwarding; useEpics params + EpicListPage search/sort controls; tests
tasks.notes: Fully independent of the events/reopen/batch work; can execute in parallel with T-001. Pure addition, no breaking change to the default list contract.

tasks.title: Epic activity timeline read endpoint and web component
tasks.description: Add an EpicQuerier event-read method that maps StoredCloudEvent (via IEventStore.ListEpicEventsAsync from T-001) to a timeline DTO exposing at least the event type, timestamp, and type-specific payload. Add HTTP GET /api/projects/{projectRef}/epics/{id}/events returning the events ordered chronologically (HTTP 200 with the list; HTTP 200 with an empty list when the epic has no events; {id} accepts internal id or number). On the web, add a getEpicEvents client method and a useEpicEvents(id) query keyed ['epics', projectId, id, 'events']; render an Activity Timeline section on EpicDetailPage that maps the event stream to human-readable entries — status change (old/new), issue link/unlink (with issue number), priority change (old/new), reopen (distinct from generic status change), and creation — each with its timestamp, and an empty state when there are no events.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /epics/{id}/events returns HTTP 200 with the epic's events ordered chronologically
GET /epics/{id}/events for an epic with no persisted events returns HTTP 200 with an empty list
Event DTOs expose at least the event type, timestamp, and the type-specific payload needed to render the timeline
{id} accepts either the epic's internal id or its number, consistent with the other epic routes
The timeline renders status changes (old/new), issue link/unlink (issue number), priority changes (old/new), reopen distinct from a generic status change, and creation
The web detail page renders the timeline section with timestamps and shows an empty state (no error) for an epic with no events
Unit/spec tests pass (server + web typecheck/test) covering read-path ordering/empty, DTO mapping for each event type, endpoint status codes, and web rendering incl. empty state
tasks.output: EpicQuerier event-read method + timeline DTOs; GET /{id}/events route; web getEpicEvents + useEpicEvents query + EpicDetailPage Activity Timeline section with empty state; tests
tasks.notes: Depends on T-001 for IEventStore.ListEpicEventsAsync and the persisted events. Tests seed events directly, so T-002/T-003 are not hard dependencies; once they land the timeline also reflects reopen and batch link/unlink events.
